mapping_method: Preserve all154 previous mappings except explicit genuine Q18 survival additions; append all9 surviving real-core questions before any expanded answers. Separate unasked key background. Reachability credit remains separate from grading requirements.
grading_scope: Judge all actually requested material facts using equivalent wording and implied actors in context. A fixed key may include explanatory background; key_context_not_required is not an additional answer requirement or tested source coverage. A response need not recite stipulated givens or a counting guard if its answer already respects them.

creator_provenance.role: Pre-test consolidation of both independently accepted map16 context corrections

questions.question: Can Blight cascade into an Ocean on a board with Ocean’s Presence? Can normal Growth Add Presence to that Ocean as if a Coastal Wetland, can it measure from existing Presence there, and how can Ocean put Presence Inland in the base game?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: Can Blight cascade into an Ocean on a board with Ocean’s Presence? Can normal Growth Add Presence to that Ocean as if a Coastal Wetland, can it measure from existing Presence there, and how can Ocean put Presence Inland in the base game?
required_facts: An active Ocean is a legal cascade destination.
Ordinary Growth cannot treat it as a Coastal Wetland for adding Presence.
Existing Ocean Presence can nevertheless originate Growth Range.
In core, Indomitable Claim can add Ocean's Presence Inland because it explicitly ignores land-type restrictions; generic adding Powers do not.

questions.question: When Ocean Drowns a Town and a City, when is Fear earned and where do pieces go? In two-Spirit play how much Energy value is a drowned City worth, can change be made, and do Dahan yield Energy?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: When Ocean Drowns a Town and a City, when is Fear earned and where do pieces go? In two-Spirit play how much Energy value is a drowned City worth, can change be made, and do Dahan yield Energy?
required_facts: Drowning a Town/City earns 1/2 Fear immediately, not when traded for Energy.
Store drowned Invaders on Ocean's panel for trade.
Trade X Health for 1 Energy, where X is Spirit count.
In two-Spirit play a City can give 1 Energy plus 1 Health change; making change is allowed.
Drowned Dahan provide no Energy.

key_context_not_required.fact: Ignore Invader Health modifiers when trading.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: The given City has no Health modifier; the question asks its ordinary two-Spirit value/change and Dahan benefit.

questions.question: Does every watery destruction count as Drowning? If Ocean’s last Presence on a board is lost mid-action, when does Ocean In Play expire and what happens to other Spirits’ Presence and surviving humans left there?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: Does every watery destruction count as Drowning? If Ocean’s last Presence on a board is lost mid-action, when does Ocean In Play expire and what happens to other Spirits’ Presence and surviving humans left there?
required_facts: Only an explicit Drown or Ocean's moved-human triggered destruction is Drowning; a thematically watery destruction is not automatically Drowning.
Ocean In Play persists through the current action tree after Ocean's last board Presence is lost.
Afterward other Spirits' nonhuman Presence remains physically but out of play until the Ocean returns.
Any surviving illegally placed humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land after triggers.

key_context_not_required.fact: Failed Drown attempts Push to non-Ocean land during their action.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: The question asks Ocean ceasing to be in play and post-tree surviving pieces; Q113 asks the separate failed-destruction Push branch.

questions.question: If a human piece remains illegally placed after an action tree, how is it cleaned up? Is that a move, destroy, remove or action, and what if no legal land exists?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: If a human piece remains illegally placed after an action tree, how is it cleaned up? Is that a move, destroy, remove or action, and what if no legal land exists?
required_facts: After the action tree, clean an illegally placed human to the nearest legal land, using judgment/physical distance if unclear.
Cleanup is not movement, Destroy, Remove or an action and triggers nothing.
If no legal land exists, return it to supply as cleanup.

key_context_not_required.fact: This correction precedes the outcome check.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: The question asks cleanup, its classification, and the no-legal-land case; it does not ask outcome-check timing.

questions.question: Bringer uses a 2-Damage Power and then a separate 1-Damage Power on an undamaged City. What happens? What if 2 then 1 Damage are instructions within a single Power, and may a Repeat pretend-destroy the same piece again?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: Bringer uses a 2-Damage Power and then a separate 1-Damage Power on an undamaged City. What happens? What if 2 then 1 Damage are instructions within a single Power, and may a Repeat pretend-destroy the same piece again?
required_facts: Separate 2- and 1-Damage Bringer Powers each fail to pretend-destroy an undamaged City and leave no hypothetical Damage.
A single Power with 2 then 1 Damage combines its instructions and pretend-destroys that City for 5 Fear without actual destruction.
A Repeat is a separate use and can pretend-destroy the same piece again if that use suffices.
Hypothetical Damage cannot combine across the original and Repeat.

questions.question: A City has 2 real Damage from another Spirit. Bringer then uses a 1-Damage Power twice via a Repeat. How much Fear does each use earn, does the City die, and is its real Damage erased?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: A City has 2 real Damage from another Spirit. Bringer then uses a 1-Damage Power twice via a Repeat. How much Fear does each use earn, does the City die, and is its real Damage erased?
required_facts: The City's 2 real Damage lets each 1-Damage nightmare use pretend-destroy it.
Each use earns 5 Fear, totaling 10.
The City survives and its existing 2 real Damage stays unchanged.

questions.question: For Bringer’s would-be destruction, what Fear and Push happens for Explorer, Town and City? Does Mists of Oblivion’s bonus for buildings actually destroyed or Vengeance of the Dead trigger from it?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: For Bringer’s would-be destruction, what Fear and Push happens for Explorer, Town and City? Does Mists of Oblivion’s bonus for buildings actually destroyed or Vengeance of the Dead trigger from it?
required_facts: Explorer pretend-destruction gives 0 Fear and Pushes the eligible Explorer if possible.
Town pretend-destruction gives 2 Fear and Pushes the eligible Town if possible.
City gives 5 Fear and no Push.
No actual destruction means no Mists destruction-based bonus or Vengeance trigger from those pretend deaths.

questions.question: Can Bringer deal real Damage by a Power saying Dahan or another Spirit deals it? Contrast Fear Cards, counterattacks after its Defend, removing/replacing Invaders, and adding Blight.

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: Can Bringer deal real Damage by a Power saying Dahan or another Spirit deals it? Contrast Fear Cards, counterattacks after its Defend, removing/replacing Invaders, and adding Blight.
required_facts: Bringer's Power's explicit Damage/Destroy remains hypothetical even if it says Dahan or another Spirit deals it.
Fear Cards deal real Damage and Dahan Ravage counterattacks remain real after Bringer's Defend.
Bringer can Remove/Replace Invaders.
Bringer can add real Blight, which destroys Presence normally.

questions.question: Can Bringer cause real destruction by reducing a damaged piece’s Health or replacing it with a lower-Health type? If Bringer pretend-destroys a Town and Pushes it into Ocean, who Drowns it and what is total Fear?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: Can Bringer cause real destruction by reducing a damaged piece’s Health or replacing it with a lower-Health type? If Bringer pretend-destroys a Town and Pushes it into Ocean, who Drowns it and what is total Fear?
required_facts: Bringer can cause real destruction indirectly when existing Damage meets lowered/new Health, including lower-Health replacement.
Ocean's separate rule Drowns the nightmare-Pushed Town.
Generate 2 Bringer Fear plus 1 actual Town destruction Fear, totaling 3.

questions.question: Can Spirits May Yet Dream flip a Fear Card already earned, on top of the deck or deeper in the deck?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: Can Spirits May Yet Dream flip a Fear Card already earned, on top of the deck or deeper in the deck?
required_facts: Spirits May Yet Dream's first effect may flip already-earned Fear cards, the top of the Fear deck, or deeper Fear cards.

questions.question: In Call on Midnight’s Dreams, which card is this Power for its Forget conditional? Must Bringer Forget a second card beyond the ordinary Major gain requirement to activate it, and can the forgotten original later be Repeated with Powerstorm?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: In Call on Midnight’s Dreams, which card is this Power for its Forget conditional? Must Bringer Forget a second card beyond the ordinary Major gain requirement to activate it, and can the forgotten original later be Repeated with Powerstorm?
required_facts: This Power means Call on Midnight's Dreams itself.
Forgetting it for the ordinary Major gain requirement also satisfies its conditional; no second Forget is required.
Once Forgotten it leaves play and cannot later be Repeated with Powerstorm's ordinary once-this-turn permission.

questions.question: When does Vengeance of the Dead trigger if one Power destroys several buildings through multiple instructions? Can its own triggered Damage trigger itself again, and how do two separately repeated Vengeance effects interact?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: When does Vengeance of the Dead trigger if one Power destroys several buildings through multiple instructions? Can its own triggered Damage trigger itself again, and how do two separately repeated Vengeance effects interact?
required_facts: Vengeance triggers after the entire destroying Power/action, not after each printed instruction.
Use the total qualifying pieces destroyed by that action.
A triggered effect cannot trigger itself, including indirectly.
Separate repeated Vengeance effects can trigger each other, but a branch stops before re-triggering the same trigger; no infinite loop.

questions.question: When an action directly grants a flexible Any Element, may its choice be delayed like an Any space on a Presence track?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: When an action directly grants a flexible Any Element, may its choice be delayed like an Any space on a Presence track?
required_facts: Choose a directly granted flexible Any Element immediately when gained.
A passive track Any may be left unchosen until later in the turn.

key_context_not_required.fact: Once a passive track Any has been chosen, it is fixed for the remainder of that turn.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: The contrast asks whether the directly gained Element choice may be delayed, like a track Any. It does not ask whether an already chosen track Element can be changed.

questions.question: A damaged Dahan leaves a land where it has bonus Health and now its Damage meets its Health. Is it destroyed in the starting land, destination or an in-between space?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: A damaged Dahan leaves a land where it has bonus Health and now its Damage meets its Health. Is it destroyed in the starting land, destination or an in-between space?
required_facts: The Dahan is destroyed in the destination after losing its bonus Health.
It retains the starting bonus until it arrives; there is no in-between location.

questions.question: When one action removes N Health worth of Invaders based on a count in a land, is the allowance split into N-sized batches? Can separate each-player Health removal allowances be pooled?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: When one action removes N Health worth of Invaders based on a count in a land, is the allowance split into N-sized batches? Can separate each-player Health removal allowances be pooled?
required_facts: A single action totals its scaled Health allowance and removes a set at or below that total; it is not split into N-sized batches.
Separate each-player removal actions cannot pool their Health allowances.

questions.question: How are Scapegoats at Terror II and III divided into actions, and what does each level destroy in each land with Towns/Cities?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: How are Scapegoats at Terror II and III divided into actions, and what does each level destroy in each land with Towns/Cities?
required_facts: Resolve one action per land with Towns/Cities, not independent actions per printed clause.
Terror II destroys one Explorer per Town plus two per City.
Terror III destroys all Explorers, then one Town per City.

questions.question: An effect must add two Blight simultaneously but only one remains on Healthy Island. What happens to that remaining Blight, when are immediate flip effects resolved, and when are the two added?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: An effect must add two Blight simultaneously but only one remains on Healthy Island. What happens to that remaining Blight, when are immediate flip effects resolved, and when are the two added?
required_facts: Flip Healthy immediately when the required simultaneous addition exceeds its pool.
Carry the remaining old Blight into the new pool.
Fully resolve immediate flipped-card effects as nested actions, including their triggers.
Then return and add the two Blight simultaneously.

key_context_not_required.fact: Add the new printed pool without setup bonus.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: The question isolates remaining-old-Blight handling, nested flip timing and addition timing, not the setup bonus or pool arithmetic; Q14 asks those.

questions.question: A Power was used Fast, then is explicitly made Slow before its ordinary Repeat. Which phase does the Repeat use? What if its text explicitly tells you to Repeat immediately?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: A Power was used Fast, then is explicitly made Slow before its ordinary Repeat. Which phase does the Repeat use? What if its text explicitly tells you to Repeat immediately?
required_facts: Ordinary Repeat uses the most recently assigned Speed, so Slow in the stated case.
An explicit immediate Repeat happens immediately after the original use regardless of phase.

questions.question: May Powers and Special Rules measure Range through Ocean as a land when Ocean In Play is active, and does that make all outside edges Coastal?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: May Powers and Special Rules measure Range through Ocean as a land when Ocean In Play is active, and does that make all outside edges Coastal?
required_facts: Powers and Special Rules can measure Range through Ocean while Ocean In Play is active.
Coastal still means touching printed Ocean; other outside edges do not become Coastal merely because they are outside edges.
